Actorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#Actor

Actor means a legal or natural person (e.g. John Doe, TNO). One actor can take on multiple roles; [CIRPASS-2 User Stories 3.1]
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/eudpp/ACTOR
Source
https://zenodo.org/records/17979585
has super-classes
has sub-classes
Legal Person c, Natural Person c
is in domain of
actor name dp, has representative mandate op, has unique operator identifier op, is notified for op, issues certificate op, performed assessment according to op, registered trade name dp, uses facility op
is in range of
conformity attested by op, has LCA verifier op, has actor op, has authorised representative op, has back-up-copy host op, has economic operator op, has issuer op, has manufacturer op, has notified body op, has responsible manufacturer op, identifies data provider op, identifies manufacturer op, is signed by op, is used by actor op, issued by op, performed by op, recorded by op, represents manufacturer op

AggregationEventc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/AggregationEvent

The event type AggregationEvent describes events that apply to objects that have been aggregated to one another. In such an event, there is a set of 'contained' objects that have been aggregated within a 'containing' entity that's meant to identify the aggregation itself. This event type is intended to be used for 'aggregations', meaning an association where there is a strong physical relationship between the containing and the contained objects such that they will all occupy the same location at the same time, until such time as they are disaggregated.
Is defined by
https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/
Term status
stable
has super-classes
EPCISEvent c
is in domain of
action dp, childEPCs op, childQuantityList op, parentID op

Area of Protectionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#AreaOfProtection

Damage area addressed by an LCIA method via the LCIA Impact Category class using the addressesAoP object property. A closed enumeration of 5 individuals.
is equivalent to
{ Human health ni , Man-made environment ni , Natural environment ni , Natural resources ni , Other AoP ni }
is in range of
addresses AoP op
has members
Human health ni, Man-made environment ni, Natural environment ni, Natural resources ni, Other AoP ni

AssociationEventc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/AssociationEvent

The event type AssociationEvent describes the association or disassociation of one or several physical objects with a parent object or a specific physical location. Like the AggregationEvent, the AssociationEvent is also used to capture associations where there is a strong physical relationship between the containing and the contained objects such that they will all occupy the same location at the same time, until such time as they are disaggregated. However, the AggregationEvent does not allow for associations of objects with physical locations; if action is DELETE while omitting the childEPC and childQuantityList field, all contained children are disaggregated from the containing parent. Because there are situations in which associations are more permanent, i.e. beyond the physical flow of goods (e.g. packing/unpacking and loading/unloading), an AssociationEvent SHOULD be used: (a) when objects need to be associated with a physical location or (b) when the parent object could also be subject to other, more temporary associations (i.e. captured using AggregationEvent).
Is defined by
https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/
Term status
stable
has super-classes
EPCISEvent c
is in domain of
action dp, childEPCs op, childQuantityList op, parentID op

BizTransactionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/BizTransaction

Document that describes a particular business transaction. An example is a specific Purchase Order or Despatch Advice. Business Transaction information may be included in EPCIS events to record an event's participation in particular business transactions.
Is defined by
https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/
Term status
stable
is in domain of
bizTransactionType op
is in range of

Environmental Footprint Scorec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#EnvironmentalFootprintScore

An aggregated single-score indicator computed as the normalised and weighted sum of a set of impact-category results. Holds one named individual eudpp:ind_EF_singleScore representing the EU Environmental Footprint single score (PEF score). The applied normalisation factors and weighting set are not modelled here as properties; they are determined by the active EF / PEF methodology version, which is resolvable via the study's eudpp:hasComplianceDeclaration link to a eudpp:ComplianceSystem source. Results computed for an EnvironmentalFootprintScore individual are eudpp:LCIAResult instances.
has super-classes
LCA Indicator c
has members
Environmental Footprint single score ni

Environmental Footprint Score Resultc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#EnvironmentalFootprintScoreResult

A normalized and weighted aggregate LCA result expressing the overall environmental performance of a product system as a single dimensionless score, computed by applying the Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) method (Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279). Aggregates the characterised results of all 16 EF 3.1 impact categories through normalization and weighting factors. Instances of this class quantify the EF single score indicator (ind_EF_singleScore, an EnvironmentalFootprintScore individual) via quantifiesIndicator.
has super-classes
LCA Result c

Inventory Indicator Resultc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#InventoryIndicatorResult

A specific LCA result representing an aggregated inventory-indicator result computed for an EN 15804+A2 inventory indicator (Table 5: resource use, waste categories, output flows). Important disambiguation: this class represents the AGGREGATED inventory-indicator value (e.g. total kg of HWD across A1-A3 for one product), as printed in EN 15804+A2 EPD tables and computed by a Method instance. It is NOT the raw flow-level life-cycle inventory (LCI) result of a process (which would be a list of elementary-flow exchanges with amounts and units, and is out of scope for this DPP-oriented LCA module).
has super-classes
LCA Result c
has sub-classes
Energy Consumption Result c, Land Use Result c, Material Footprint c, Recycled Materials Use Result c, Sustainable Renewable Materials Use Result c, Water Consumption Result c

has inventory indicator result op

Land Use Resultc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#LandUseResult

An LCA result quantifying impacts associated with land occupation and transformation in a product system. Commonly associated with the EN 15804+A2 land use indicator (LU), which is characterised under EF 3.1. No formal quantifiesIndicator restriction is imposed; note that LU sits at the boundary between inventory and impact in EN 15804 and may be refined in future ontology versions.
has super-classes

LCA Indicatorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#LCAIndicator

Abstract umbrella class for an indicator definition (impact or inventory category) that an eudpp:Method calculates values for. Each instance identifies exactly one method under which it is computed; this constraint is formalised as owl:maxCardinality 1 on eudpp:computedByMethod. Note: an indicator individual is the indicator DEFINITION (e.g. "FW – Net use of fresh water, in m3"); a numerical value computed for that indicator on a specific study is an eudpp:LCAResult instance (LCIAResult or InventoryIndicatorResult).

LCA Methodc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#LCAMethod

A life-cycle assessement method that produces values for one indicator from an inventory of elementary flows. Covers both (a) characterised LCIA methods (which apply characterisation factors to compute a midpoint impact result), and (b) inventory aggregation methods (which sum / aggregate inventory flows to produce an inventory-indicator result, e.g. the EN 15804+A2 inventory indicators FW, HWD, PERE etc. defined as inventory-level by the standard's calculation rules).

LCA Resultc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#LCAResult

Abstract class for any LCA computation output of a study. Has three subclasses: eudpp:LCIAResult (characterised impact result) which applies characterisation factors of an LCIA method, eudpp:InventoryIndicatorResult (aggregated inventory-indicator result) whcih is a sum/aggregation over the inventory without characterisation, and eudpp:EnvironmentalFootprintScoreResult which represents the aggregated EF single score result. In the regulatory sense of ESPR Art. 2(24), some characterized individuals of LCAResult constitute environmental footprints — quantifications of environmental impacts of a product throughout its life cycle.Other LCAResult instances, however, fall outside the strict ESPR definition. For this reason, LCAResult is linked to the ESPR "Environmental Footprint" concept via skos:broadMatch rather than owl:equivalentClass.

LCIA Impact Indicatorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#LCIAImpactIndicator

A characterised impact indicator outside the EN 15804+A2 selection — direct subclass of eudpp:LCAIndicator, sibling of eudpp:EN15804Indicator. Holds the 16 official EF 3.1 / PEF impact category indicators as named individuals (Andreasi Bassi et al., JRC, 2023). These are the impact indicators used by general LCA studies (eudpp:LCAStudy) following the EU Environmental Footprint method, distinct from the EN 15804+A2 set used by EPDStudy. The two sets overlap conceptually — both have e.g. a "Climate change" indicator with kg CO2-eq — but differ operationally: EN 15804+A2 splits Climate change into four sub-indicators (total, fossil, biogenic, luluc) and selects 6 "with caveats" indicators with EN-specific reporting rules; EF 3.1 keeps Climate change as one indicator and presents 16 categories at one aggregation level.

Material Footprintc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#MaterialFootprint

An InventoryIndicatorResult that "refers to the total amount of raw materials extracted to meet final consumption demands" (ESPR Art. 2(26)). Modelled as an inventory-level result rather than a characterised LCIA result, as it aggregates raw material extraction flows without applying characterisation factors. No single EN 15804+A2 inventory indicator individual is pinned via quantifiesIndicator; the link is left to individual instances, as material footprint spans multiple EN 15804+A2 resource use inventory indicators (PERE, PENRE, SM, RSF, NRSF, etc.).

Substance of concernc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#SubstanceOfConcern

A substance that: (a) meets the criteria laid down in Article 57 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 and is identified in accordance with Article 59(1) of that Regulation; (b) is classified in Part 3 of Annex VI to Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 in one of the following hazard classes or hazard categories: (i) carcinogenicity categories 1 and 2; (ii) germ cell mutagenicity categories 1 and 2; (iii) reproductive toxicity categories 1 and 2; (iv) endocrine disruption for human health categories 1 and 2; (v) endocrine disruption for the environment categories 1 and 2; (vi) persistent, mobile and toxic or very persistent, very mobile properties; (vii) persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic or very persistent, very bioaccumulative properties; (viii) respiratory sensitisation category 1; (ix) skin sensitisation category 1; (x) hazardous to the aquatic environment — categories chronic 1 to 4; (xi) hazardous to the ozone layer; (xii) specific target organ toxicity — repeated exposure categories 1 and 2; (xiii) specific target organ toxicity — single exposure categories 1 and 2; (c) is regulated under Regulation (EU) 2019/1021; or (d) negatively affects the reuse and recycling of materials in the product in which it is present.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/SOC
Source
http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj

Substance presencec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#SubstancePresence

A contextual relation entity representing the presence of a substance in relation to a product as placed on the market, including a product, component or spare part. It enables product-dependent location, concentration and instruction information to be represented without treating those data as intrinsic characteristics of the substance itself or classifying the presence as a product property. In the CORE profile the modelling pattern is one SubstancePresence per reported location when different locations require different concentrations; sector-specific extensions may provide explicit reference bases for several calculation perspectives. This class is an ontology modelling abstraction supporting ESPR Article 7(5), rather than a term explicitly defined by the Regulation.

has LCA verifierop back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#hasLCAVerifier

Links a review to the independent, third-party actor responsible for validating the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) or Environmental Product Declaration (EPD). Verifier means a person or organisation that carries out the independent verification of an EPD or LCA study, i.e. confirms through objective evidence that the specified requirements are fulfilled, e.g. the PCR and EN 15804+A2. It also covers the critical reviewer of an LCA study and the verifier of a PEF study. Independent verification may be internal or external; EPDs for business-to-consumer communication require third-party verification, also comparative assertions under ISO 14040 and any comparisons under the European Commission’s ILCD Handbook. The type of verification is recorded on the Review (TypeOfReview). ILCD: reviewer (1-3-20-87); [ISO 14025:2006, 3.8, adapted] Review is modelled in the EU DPP CO LCA module. Actor is modelled in the EU DPP CO ACTOR module.
Source
https://www.iso.org/standard/87610.html

Review c
has range
Actor c

eventTimeZoneOffsetdp back to ToC or Data Property ToC

IRI: https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/eventTimeZoneOffset

The time zone offset in effect at the time and place the event occurred, expressed as an offset from UTC. The value of this field SHALL be a string consisting of the character '+' or the character '-', followed by two digits whose value is within the range 00 through 14 (inclusive), followed by a colon character ':', followed by two digits whose value is within the range 00 through 59 (inclusive), except that if the value of the first two digits is 14, the value of the second two digits must be 00. For example, the value +05:30 specifies that where the event occurred, local time was five hours and 30 minutes later than UTC (that is, midnight UTC was 5:30am local time).
Is defined by
https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/

uomdp back to ToC or Data Property ToC

IRI: https://ref.gs1.org/epcis/uom

(Optional) Unit of measure by which the specified value(s) of the property specified by type should be interpreted. If there is no value, minValue, maxValue, averageValue or percValue field present, uom SHALL be omitted. When a uom field is present, its value SHALL be the 2- or 3-character code for a physical unit specified in the 'Common Code' column of UN/CEFACT Recommendation'20 [CEFACT20]. Note: GS1 provides a tool containing a machine-readable file which enables the automatic conversion between quantitative values expressed using UN/CEFACT common codes. source statusap back to ToC or Annotation Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#sourceStatus

Annotation property used to state the epistemic or normative status of the source for an ontology resource, for example direct legal definition, explicit legal information element, ESPR-grounded modelling abstraction, or JRC draft proposal. It is intentionally distinct from dcterms:provenance, which is reserved for ownership and custody history.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/eudpp/SOC
Source
https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/terms/provenance/

source vocabularyap back to ToC or Annotation Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#sourceVocabulary

Provenance annotation identifying the vocabulary, standard, or ontology from which a class, property, or named individual of this ontology aligns with. Possible values: "LCA ontology" (introduced by this ontology, no direct external counterpart), "ILCD base" (corresponds to the ILCD base data format), "ILCD+EPD extension" (corresponds to the ILCD+EPD v1.3 extension, InData epd/epd2/epd24 namespaces), "Dublin Core" (aligned with dcterms), "PROV-O" (aligned with W3C Provenance Ontology), "SKOS" (aligned with W3C Simple Knowledge Organization System), "FOAF" (aligned with Friend of a Friend vocabulary), "LCAnet" (aligned with the LCAnet ontology).

LCA or EPD verifierni back to ToC or Named Individual ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/eudpp#lcaVerifier

Verifier means a person or organisation that carries out the independent verification of an EPD or LCA study, i.e. confirms through objective evidence that the specified requirements are fulfilled, e.g. the PCR and EN 15804+A2. It also covers the critical reviewer of an LCA study and the verifier of a PEF study. Independent verification may be internal or external; EPDs for business-to-consumer communication require third-party verification, also comparative assertions under ISO 14040 and any comparisons under the European Commission’s ILCD Handbook. The type of verification is recorded on the Review (TypeOfReview). ILCD: reviewer (1-3-20-87); [ISO 14025:2006, 3.8, adapted]
Source
https://www.iso.org/standard/87610.html
belongs to
Role c
has facts
